      <title>Nottingham Forest 0-1 Arsenal: Premier League – as it happened</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2026/oct/18/nottingham-forest-v-arsenal-premier-league-live</link>
      <description><p>A late, deflected winner from Noni Madueke gave Arsenal a vital win in a low-quality game, Forest then missing two good chances to equalise</p><p><strong>Forest will want – and probably need – to make this game a mess.</strong> If it’s open and played through midfield, Arsenal will open them up because, with the guile they’ve added by buying Guimaraes, along with an in-form Odegaard, they have the ability to exploit space. For that reason, Forest need bodies everywhere, especially in the middle of the pitch, forcing them wide, where Saka might just’ve lost the spring in his acceleration following last season’s achilles injury while, on the other side, Eze isn’t going to go on the outside.</p><p><strong>Elsewhere, 10-man Sunderland trail Bournemouth 2-0 with seconds remaining,</strong> while Brighton have splattered Palace 5-0 to move second above Arsenal, their goal difference +18. Ridiculous behaviour.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2026/oct/18/nottingham-forest-v-arsenal-premier-league-live">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Madueke breaks Nottingham Forest’s resistance as dogged Arsenal edge to victory</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/18/nottingham-forest-arsenal-premier-league-match-report</link>
      <description><p>The theme before kick-off was blanks. Or, more precisely, whether either team could stop firing them at the City Ground. It was a detail to make Oliver Glasner extremely uncomfortable that his Nottingham Forest team had still to score at their own stadium this season. Arsenal, meanwhile, <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jan/17/nottingham-forest-arsenal-premier-league-match-report">had drawn 0-0</a> on their previous two visits to this part of the east Midlands. They had only one win in five here.</p><p>Forest’s frustrations under their new manager go on. It was another spirited performance from them, bits to like, especially a full-throttle performance from Liam Delap in the No 9 position. But, for the fifth time under Glasner, there was not a goal to celebrate in front of the home support.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/18/nottingham-forest-arsenal-premier-league-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Bournemouth’s, and Marco Rose’s, wait for a Premier League win is over.       <title>Gómez halfway-line wondergoal sparks Brighton’s 5-0 thrashing of sorry Crystal Palace</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/18/brighton-crystal-palace-premier-league-match-report</link>
      <description><p>At last, Fabian Hürzeler has the scalp that matters most to all Brighton fans and in humiliating fashion. Diego Gómez’s breathtaking goal-of-the-season contender from the halfway line, à la David Beckham, was the highlight of another hugely impressive performance from the Premier League’s top scorers as they continued their flying start to the season.</p><p>Not since a 4-1 thrashing here in February 2024 under Roberto De Zerbi had Brighton tasted victory against their arch rivals from up the A23 – a run of four matches. But having been handed the initiative by Jaydee Canvot’s own goal, a stunned Palace found themselves 3-0 down after 10 minutes. It got even worse for Pierre Sage after Brighton extended their lead through Gómez’s wonderstrike and Yasin Ayari, with Charalampos Kostoulas adding a fourth after half-time and the substitute Jack Hinshelwood’s late strike matching their record 5-0 win over Palace from 1956 in Division Three South.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/18/brighton-crystal-palace-premier-league-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>
